label: Metabarons
description: Metabarons lorepack for faithful Sans-Nom prototype play: dynasty pressure, body law, taboo, refusal, spectacle, and philosophical consequence.
game_synopsis: The player stands inside the Metabaron dynasty's pressure field, where family, body, weapon, memory, service, and public consequence decide legitimacy. The opening story stages one immediate household crisis that forces the player to choose how inheritance, obedience, refusal, love, or sacrifice should mean anything when witnesses are watching.
protagonist_role: A contested figure bound to the dynasty's household machinery: heir, sworn servant, weapon-keeper, witness, lover, rival, or survivor whose legitimacy is under pressure.
opening_situation: A household demand turns private lineage truth into public consequence while someone close to the player needs an answer now.
initial_pressure: The opening demands an irreversible visible cost before the player fully understands which family memory, duty, or betrayal is being exposed.
story_lines: Move through a household crisis where legitimacy depends on visible cost, witnessed action, and family memory.
Decide whether inheritance means obedience to the dynasty, refusal of the dynasty, transformation of its purpose, or service to someone it has harmed.
Navigate servants, witnesses, rivals, lovers, weapons, and family figures whose loyalty is real but never simple.
Make choices whose consequences are public, bodily, and remembered by the household.
must_honor: The dynasty treats family, body, weapon, memory, and duty as inseparable.
Power is proven through visible cost rather than private intention.
Refusal matters only when it risks love, status, body, or succession.
Witnesses and servants are not scenery; they shape memory, legitimacy, and consequence.
Violence should carry philosophical and emotional pressure, not exist as spectacle alone.
must_not_violate: Do not make dynasty duty consequence-free or purely decorative.
Do not turn the story into generic space fantasy detached from lineage, body, ritual, and inheritance.
Do not resolve family pressure with simple rebellion that costs nothing.
Do not flatten servants, lovers, parents, or rivals into exposition devices.
Do not offer choices that only navigate locations without changing duty, knowledge, loyalty, or cost.
choice_principles: Each major choice should express a stance toward inheritance, obedience, refusal, love, or bodily sacrifice.
Choices should expose what the heir values under pressure, then make the household react.
A good branch changes who witnesses the heir, what proof exists, or what cost becomes unavoidable.
Lore fidelity matters more than novelty; surprise should come from staging and consequence inside the dynasty contract.

source_events: Dynasty legitimacy is repeatedly tested through bodily cost, family obedience, refusal, weapon inheritance, and public consequence.
Servants, witnesses, and narrators shape how family violence becomes remembered truth.
must_include_canon_facts: The playable story must preserve the Metabaron dynasty as a world where family duty, bodily proof, weapon legitimacy, and remembered consequence are inseparable.
allowed_original_insertions: New household figures, servants, rivals, witnesses, and local rites may be created when they do not replace or contradict established dynasty logic.
The player may be an internal original figure whose crisis exposes canon-faithful pressures rather than retelling a specific volume beat.
